candidate_requirements.requirement: Ask about ingestion of hair or other non-food material, its chronology and whether stopping was actually verified.
candidate_requirements.rationale: An upper abdominal mass with poor intake warrants a focused ingestion/behaviour history without requiring knowledge of the eventual diagnosis.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: A non-judgmental pica, hair ingestion or foreign-body history, including who observed it and any follow-up. Exact diagnostic vocabulary is unnecessary.
candidate_requirements.deadline: Before the final assessment, within the six question turns. Emergency escalation must not be delayed to exhaust the question budget.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Request examination and anatomical assessment of the mass or signs of obstruction/peritoneal irritation.
candidate_requirements.rationale: A palpable paediatric abdominal mass requires localisation and assessment for complications.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Focused examination plus appropriate imaging/paediatric gastroenterology or surgical assessment; asking for the available CT is one accepted route. Do not require immediate endoscopy as the only adequate request.
candidate_requirements.deadline: Before the final assessment, within the six question turns. Emergency escalation must not be delayed to exhaust the question budget.

candidate_requirements.rationale: Pallor and poor appetite are visible reasons to investigate blood loss, iron status and malnutrition.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Blood count with appropriate iron/bleeding evaluation and nutritional assessment, or an equivalent paediatric evaluation. Exhaustive micronutrient testing is unnecessary.
candidate_requirements.deadline: Before the final assessment, within the six question turns. Emergency escalation must not be delayed to exhaust the question budget.
